full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 was issued on 18-03-98 at the instance of the accused petitioners, Doctor Mominur Rahman alias Zinna and Jostshna Begum calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the accused petitioners should not be enlarged on anticipatory bail in connection with Kotwali PS Case No. 3(1)98 pending in the court of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Bishesh Adalat, Mymensingh. 

 2. Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2036 of 1998 was issued on 1-4-98 at the instance of the accused petitioner Doctor AKM Moqsudul Hassan calling upon the opposite parties to cause as to why he should not be enlarged on anticipatory bail in Special Case No. 224/1997 pending before the Special Tribunal, Mymensingh. 

 4. Informant Roni Akhter lodged FIR on 5-1-98 alleging that on the previous midnight she n was called by the accused Jostshna for going to the room of accused doctor Mominur Rahman, alias Zinna and she took her to that room and then she closed the door from outside and the accused Zinna had raped her against her will, In that case charge sheet was submitted under sections 6(1) and 14 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain 1995 and in the charge-sheet both the accused were shown as absconding and the Investigating Officer  prayed for issuance of warrant of arrest and proclamation and attachment order against them. Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 49 of 1998 was started in the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Bishesh Bidhan Adalat against the petitioners of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 after receipt of the record by that Adalat. While so absconding they surrendered before this Court on 18-3-98 arid were allowed ad-interim anticipatory bail on the ground that the case was engineered by the business rivals and enemies of the petitioner No. 1 to destroy his name and fame and professional image out of business rivalry over medical clinic business and police is behind the petitioners and if they were arrested they would be seriously manhandled for obtaining confession from them and the case has been filed against them so that they could not get any relief from the lower Court. 

 5. Complainant Masuma Sultana was married to the accused petitioner doctor AKM Maqsudul Hassan in 1982 and they have two daughters. He is a medical officer of Titulia Health Centre. Due to domestic trouble his wife left his residence on 27-9-97. Thereafter he filed GR Case No. 1931 of 1997 against his wife complainant Masuma Sultana alleging theft of property. Thereafter on 2-10-97 he divorced his wife who filed complaint Case No. 2119 of 97 under section 10(2) of the said Ain against the ace alleging that he attempted to cause her death by torture over the demand of dowry. The case was sent to the police and after investigation police submitted final report on 9-11-97 and thereafter the case was sent to the Bishesh Adalat and registered as Case No. 211 of 1997 and on 19-11-97 accused petitioner was discharged by the said Bishesh Adalat. Thereafter on 23-11-97 his wife Masuma Sultana filed a petition of complaint before the Bishesh Adalat alleging that case filed by her before the Magistrate was amicably settled and thereafter she was taken in the house of the accused petitioner where on 14-11-97 accused petitioner again over the demand of dowry assaulted her with wooden ruler and had broken her left hand. After examining her on oath Bishesh Adalat took cognizance against the accused petitioner under section 11 of the said Ain and directed to issue warrant of arrest against the accused-petitioner and fixed 7-1-98 for his appearance. Without surrendering before the Bishesh Adalat petitioner surrendered before this Court on 1-4-98 on the ground that the case has been started against him to unnecessarily harass him and to damage his reputation in his profession and there is no other forum except this Hon'ble Court for anticipatory bail and finding no other alternative to save his dignity, reputation, prestige and life he had surrendered before this Court and prayed for ad interim bail. 

 6. Learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1988 submitted that to avoid harassment in the Rand of the police they surrendered before this Court with prayer for anticipatory bail and on 5-5-98 their bail was cancelled by Bishesh Adalat and warrant of arrest was issued against them and after their surrender on the very same day Bishesh Adalat enlarged them on bail and, as such, they are no longer on bail granted by this court but they are on bail granted by the Bishesh Adalat and hence the Rule has become infructuous. 

 7. Learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2036 of 1998 submitted that the case was filed by the divorced wife of the petitioner to unnecessarily harass him only four days after his discharge from the earlier case and the complainant being influential in the locality was in a position to influence police and district administration and as such, petitioner apprehended that his life was at stake at Mymensingh and so he surrendered before this Court finding no other alternative with a prayer for anticipatory bail. 

 9. Learned Advocate appearing for the added opposite party Mrs Rokeya Kabir as well as the informant Rony Akhter also opposed the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 making similar submissions at length. Main thrust of that submission is that if the highest Court of the country remains insensitive to the social realities and goes on granting anticipatory bail to the persons accused of heinous crimes on insufficient ground the purpose of enacting laws for suppressing crimes against women and children would go on increasing frustrating the object of such laws. 

 10. Learned Advocate for the complainant opposite party No. 2 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2036 of 1998 submitted after producing a copy of the police report dated 8-11-97 submitted in the theft case filed by the petitioner against the opposite party No. 2 that police submitted final report in both the counter cases as there was amicable compromise between them before submission of final reports and as such, allegation of compromise in the petition of complaint is not without foundation. 

 11. On going through the FIR and charge sheet submitted against the accused petitioners of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 we find that they have been accused of committing offence under section 6, 11 and 14 of the said Ain which is punishable with death or imprisonment for life. Bishesh Adalat framed charge against the petitioners on 6-4-98 under the aforesaid provisions of the said Ain and some of the witnesses including the informant have been examined by the Court in the meantime. 

 12. On going through the petition of complaint filed in Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 224 of 1997 we find that allegations of assaulting the complainant by the accused-petitioner of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2036 of 1998 and breaking her left hand over the demand of dowry have been made and the Bishesh Adalat took cognizance against the accused petitioner under section 11 of the said Ain which is punishable With imprisonment for life or imprisonment upto 14 years which shall not be less than 5 years. Before the petitioners/petitioner enter upon defence and adduce evidence it is not possible at this stage to decide which version of the case is true or false. 

 13. In the case of Belayet Hossain Sharif vs. State reported in 18 BID 172 to which one of us is a party it was observed: 

 14. Let us now see whether petitioners of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 have been able to satisfy this Court about their ground for not surrendering before the Court below. 

 15. It appears from the present address of the two petitioners given in the cause title of the application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure upon which Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 was issued that they are residing in Mymensingh town and they managed to obtain the exact copy of the FIR from the local police. Though clinic of the petitioner No. 1 was sealed by the police after the lodging of the FIR petitioners were not arrested in spite of their residing in Mymensingh town. Moreover, one month before the date of their surrender charge-sheet was submitted against them and as such, allegation of their apprehension of mishandling them by police for obtaining confession from them after the submission of charge-sheet does not appear to us to have any foundation. Though none of the parties produced copy of the entire order-sheet of the Court below it can easily be presumed that before they surrendered before this Court the case record was received by the Court below and possibly warrant of arrest and proclamation and attachment as prayed for by the police was issued by the Court below . In the above facts and circumstances we find no cogent reason on their part for not surrendering before the Magistrate after lodging of the FIR and sealing of petitioner No 1's clinic by the police and before the Bishesh Adalat after submission of charge-sheet and receipt of the record by that Court. 

 16. Though according to the petitioner of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2036 of 1998 the case was started by his wife against him before the Bishesh Adalat on the basis of concocted and frivolous allegations there is no explanation why he did not surrender before the Bishesh Adalat which issued warrant of arrest against him and fixed 7-1-98 for his appearance. There is no basis for the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2036 of 1998 that the complainant is in a position to influence the local police and the district administration or that petitioner's life at Mymensingh was at stake. There is no allegation that due to activities of the police petitioner could not attend his duties in the Titulia Health Centre. 

 17. In the above facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the petitioners/petitioner of the respective Rule could not satisfy us with cogent reason and materials the cause for not surrendering before the Court below. From the materials on record we find no agility or over zealousness on the part of the police to arrest and not to speak of harassing them as alleged. Rather it appears from the facts and circumstances of the two cases that they had been residing at their respective residence and petitioner doctor AKM Moqsudul Hasan had been attending his office before they were enlarged on ad interim bail without being harassed by the police. 

 18. We refrain from considering the submission made by the learned Advocate for added opposite party Mrs Rokeya Kabir on the question of desirability of granting anticipatory bail to persons accused of heinous crimes like women repression as the very same question is pending before the Appellate Division in an appeal preferred by the State against granting of ad interim anticipatory bail to the petitioners of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998. 

 19. Though the Bishesh Adalat cancelled bail of the two petitioners in Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 49 of 1998 on 5-5-98 and subsequently allowed them bail on that very date and though application of the informant was heard on 18-5-98 in presence of the learned Advocate of the petitioners, he did not inform us that the Rule has become infructuous in view of the aforesaid order of the Bishesh Adalat. This question has been raised only yesterday when the Rule is being seriously contested by Government as well as added opposite party. 

 20. In view of the above let us now consider orders dated 5-5-98 passed by the Bishesh Adalat. It appears from the orderNo. 8 dated 5-5-98 that as the petitioners did not file any hazira warrant of arrest was directed to be issued against them, It appears from the subsequent order No.9 dated 5-5-98 that the petitioners filed hazira and prayed for bail. Bishesh Adalat considering the submission of their lawyer that there was some delay on their part in coming to the Court they were allowed bail with the observation that they have been granted bail by the High Court Division and they were enjoying the privilege of that bail. Thus it appears that by the earlier order bail granted to them by this court was not cancelled by Bishesh Adalat. But only warrant of arrest was ordered to be issued against them as they did not file hazira. The said Bishesh Adalat did not grant them bail on consideration of the merit of the case and they were granted bail on the ground that they were enjoying privilege of the bail granted by this Court. Thus it appears to us that by the subsequent order No.9 the earlier order No.8 directing issuance of warrant of arrest was merely recalled and Bishesh Adalat did not allow the petitioners bail on consideration of the merit of the case. In such circumstances Bishesh Adalat was not justified in accepting bail bonds from the petitioners. 

 21. When an accused is enlarged on ad-interim bail granted by this Court during pendency of the Rule, a court subordinate to this Court has no authority to cancel the ad-interim bail granted by this Court. Such a court may bring the misuse of privilege of such bail to the notice of this Court which is in seisin of the matter till disposal of the Rule. If such misuse of the privilege of the bail is brought to the notice of this Court during pendency of the Rule this Court would certainly take into consideration such fact in disposing of the Rule. Only after disposal of a Rule confirming the ad interim bail by this court a subordinate court would be competent to cancel the bail for misusing the privilege of such bail granted by this Court as this Court is no longer in seisin of the matter after disposal of the Rule. It appears that Bishesh Adalat was conscious about the above position and did not cancel the bail of the petitioners by order No. 8 dated 5-5-98 and merely directed issuance of warrant of arrest for compelling their attendance before that Adalat. In view of the same we find no merit in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1554 of 1998 has become infructuous and they are enjoying the privilege of bail granted by the Court below.
